title: Anti-Money Laundering Amendment (Gaming Machine Venues) Bill 2012 [2013]
short_title: Anti-Money Laundering Amendment (Gaming Machine Venues) Bill 2012 [2013]

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would bring specified poker machine payments under federal anti-money laundering reporting rules and require venues to pay amounts above $1,000 by cheque.
A payout over $1,000, or cashing a payout cheque transferred between people, would become a threshold transaction requiring a report in the approved form.
The cheque requirement would cover both winnings and unplayed credits, and the amendments would begin on the day following royal assent to the bill.
changes: Controllers of eligible gaming machine venues would become designated service providers when making credit payments in the circumstances covered by the amendment.
Payout cheques would have to identify that they were issued for gaming machine winnings or credits.
Failure to follow the cheque payment requirement would carry a penalty of two years' imprisonment or 120 penalty units.
summary.affected: Controllers of eligible gaming machine venues, players receiving payouts and people cashing transferred payout cheques are affected.
